paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes a training-free inference-time method for efficient interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning.
dominant_domain: Multimodal reasoning, visually grounded reasoning, efficient interleaved visual-text chain-of-thought.
must_cover: DaP-ICoT addresses two ICoT limits: static visual insertion and broken visual representations.
DVTI uses logit-margin confidence to decide whether a visual thought is needed.
PVTG uses SAM2 object segmentation and attention-based relevance to choose a coherent object image.
Main results span M3CoT, ScienceQA, and MME across five MLLMs.
Efficiency evidence includes 314 average tokens and a 72.6% reduction compared with ICoT.
key_numbers: Chameleon-7B M3CoT zero-shot: DaP-ICoT 41.0 vs SCAFFOLD 31.0 and ICoT 26.1.
Qwen2-VL-7B: M3CoT 57.2/58.7, ScienceQA 75.9/78.5, MME 2012.2/2076.0 under zero-shot/one-shot.
Ablation on Qwen2-VL-7B: full 57.2 and 75.9; without PVTG 43.4 and 55.5; without DVTI 42.8 and 55.1.
Token accounting: DaP-ICoT 314 average tokens vs ICoT 1,146, CCoT 1,294, DDCoT 1,426.
Image usage: DaP-ICoT inserts about 1.2 images per sample vs ICoT about 2.6; average inserted image tokens about 26.
Confidence: DaP-ICoT improves confidence in 80.7% of samples vs ICoT 46.4%.
Threshold search: tau equals 0.2 yields 57.2% zero-shot and 58.7% one-shot on M3CoT with Qwen2-VL-7B.
real_comparisons: Compared with ICoT, DaP-ICoT changes fixed per-step visual insertion into confidence-triggered insertion.
Compared with ICoT patch-level visual snippets, DaP-ICoT uses SAM2 object-level candidates to reduce broken visual thoughts.
Compared with CCoT and DDCoT, DaP-ICoT reports lower token consumption while retaining stronger M3CoT results.
Compared with DeepScan and REALM in the local Reasoning map, DaP-ICoT is still an inference-time evidence insertion method, but the evidence unit is an object image inside interleaved CoT.

central_claims.claim: Dynamic visual insertion improves both effectiveness and efficiency over fixed ICoT insertion.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The method can reduce redundant visual insertion and improves reported benchmark results under the authors' evaluation settings.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove that the same threshold will generalize without tuning to every dataset, model family, or deployment setting.

central_claims.claim: Object-level visual guidance is more useful than fragmented visual token selection.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The PVTG ablation and qualitative case support the claim that coherent object images help the tested models.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not isolate whether gains come from semantic completeness, SAM2 quality, or extra object-centric preprocessing.

central_claims.claim: DaP-ICoT is a training-free route for more efficient thinking with images.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The method is implemented as inference-time control and reports lower inserted visual content cost.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It is not tool-free because PVTG relies on SAM2 segmentation and attention-based matching.

claim_boundaries: State-of-the-art claims are scoped to the listed reproduced baselines, models, and three benchmarks.
Efficiency is measured through token accounting and insertion frequency, not full wall-clock latency or segmentation overhead.
The method remains training-free for the MLLM parameters, but it uses external segmentation for object candidates.
The confidence threshold is tuned on M3CoT validation data, so threshold transfer is an open question.
negative_or_limiting_results: Figure 7 indicates performance degrades at overly high thresholds after tau passes the moderate range.
Removing PVTG causes a large drop, showing the method is sensitive to visual selection quality.
Removing DVTI causes a similar drop, showing the method depends on the confidence trigger rather than simply adding better crops.
The paper does not report detailed segmentation failure cases or runtime cost for SAM2.
mechanism_result_map: DVTI confidence threshold maps to reduced image insertion and 72.6% lower token consumption.
PVTG object-level selection maps to stronger ablation results and the Figure 8 qualitative correction.
The combination of DVTI and PVTG maps to full-table gains across Chameleon, LLaVA, and Qwen2-VL backbones.
Confidence improvement analysis maps inserted visual content to higher model certainty after visual insertion.
comparative_positioning: In the Reasoning TrainingFree branch, DaP-ICoT is the efficiency-oriented successor to ICoT.
Relative to DeepScan, DaP-ICoT does not perform hierarchical search; it controls when and what to insert into CoT.
Relative to REALM, DaP-ICoT stays in 2D visual reasoning rather than 3DGS multi-view reasoning.
Relative to train-side papers such as PFlowNet or DeepEyes, DaP-ICoT does not change model parameters.
reuse_takeaways: Use logit margin as a cheap internal uncertainty signal for when to call visual evidence.
Use complete object crops rather than scattered patch tokens when inserting images into reasoning.
Report both accuracy and visual-token cost when claiming thinking-with-images improvements.
For future 3D agent work, map DVTI-style triggers to when the agent should request a new view, crop, or 3D render.
followup_questions: How much of the gain remains if SAM2 object proposals are noisy or unavailable?
Does tau learned on M3CoT transfer to MME or other fine-grained benchmarks without retuning?
What is the true wall-clock tradeoff after adding segmentation and object matching overhead?
Can the confidence trigger be calibrated per model rather than searched per validation set?

Separate the real contribution into insertion timing, object-level representation, and evaluation discipline.
Compress DaP-ICoT into a local Reasoning-map statement about efficient inference-time visual evidence insertion.
Explain why previous ICoT is inefficient and semantically broken when it inserts visual content at every step.
Define the evaluated benchmarks, backbones, baselines, settings, metrics, and threshold tuning protocol.
Trace the execution chain from confidence estimation to visual insertion and object-level interleaved reasoning.
Use Table 1 and Figures 3 to 6 to connect accuracy, ablation, token use, insertion frequency, and confidence.
Assess what the method truly proves, why the numbers hold, and where threshold and segmentation dependence may limit claims.
List the concrete overclaim risks: validation-tuned threshold, SAM2 dependence, limited latency accounting, and unclear failure analysis.
